one_line: Agent-native workspace for governed tax evidence and reversible document actions.
what_it_does: Lets external agents discover tax-document tools, search and retrieve canonical evidence, answer governed tax questions, and perform reversible document management alongside a visible library.
leverage_rationale: Structured evidence access, shared document state, citations, and revision-safe reversible actions materially outperform brittle UI driving for tax work.
leverage_evidence: About text describes seven WebMCP capabilities for discovery, evidence retrieval, reasoning, and reversible actions.
Video frames show a populated document/conversation workspace with a distinct agent execution panel.
execution_rationale: The stated workflow covers evidence search, cited tax reasoning, rename/trash/restore, and revision verification; frames show a populated coherent application, though small text limits direct verification.
execution_evidence: Frames show loaded comments/document UI and a populated agent-side activity panel.
Packet reports live demo and 13 active documents plus trash state.
impact_rationale: Tax practitioners and sole proprietors have a concrete high-stakes need for organized, governed evidence and traceable workflows.
impact_evidence: Packet describes Kenyan sole-proprietor tax question with citations, warnings, and conversation state.
Document discovery and canonical evidence retrieval address manual handoff friction.
creativity_rationale: Treating tax work as an inspectable agent workspace with governed evidence and reversible records is a strong, thoughtful interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent-native tax workspace framing and governed knowledge workflow.
Restore recovers original filename after a reversible trash action.
usability_note: Visible library plus agent panel and reversible actions suggest good human oversight; detailed controls are small in the contact sheet.
red_flags: Frame text is low resolution and does not independently expose exact tool calls.
standouts: Strong shared-state and reversibility story for a consequential domain.
advance_reason: High-impact, deeply WebMCP-relevant workflow with substantial evidence and coherent scope.

one_line: Shared pixel-art canvas where humans and agents create and refine game assets.
what_it_does: Provides a browser pixel-art workspace for generating, editing, animating, organizing, and exporting game-ready assets through shared human and agent tools.
leverage_rationale: Live canvas context, selected frame, palette, viewport, and one shared undo stack make precise agent collaboration materially better than copying images through generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Packet says agents inspect and edit the same live artwork and share undo history.
Frames show agent-guided generation progressing to organized character and animation galleries.
execution_rationale: The contact sheet shows a progression from prompt to multiple characters and animation-ready asset sets; editing/export steps are claimed more than directly shown.
execution_evidence: Frames visibly show landing, generated character galleries, sprite frames, and a new project state.
Packet reports browser-native workspace, palettes, animation frames, and export.
impact_rationale: Indie game developers and artists have a real bottleneck converting attractive generations into consistent editable assets; this targets that gap directly.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies palette consistency, usable animation frames, and cleanup as the target problem.
Frames show multiple characters and motion sets rather than a single image.
creativity_rationale: The collaborative editable-canvas model is a fresh synthesis beyond image vending, with generation pursued into production-oriented sprites and animation.
creativity_evidence: Shared human/agent canvas and undo stack.
Reference-conditioned, masked, directional, and skeleton-based asset workflows are described.
usability_note: Prompt-led flow and visible galleries appear approachable; detailed pixel editing controls are not legible in the contact sheet.
red_flags: Exact WebMCP calls and export completion are not clearly visible.
standouts: Strong shared-canvas collaboration concept with concrete game-asset outputs.
advance_reason: Distinctive, useful creative workflow with visible output and meaningful agent delta.

one_line: Shared caseboard for finding, comparing, and citing archived webpage evidence.
what_it_does: Scopes historical questions across public archives, finds capture windows, compares archived diffs, and pins cited findings for human review and export.
leverage_rationale: Structured archive discovery, bounded capture windows, and shared cited case state are central to reliable historical investigation and difficult to replicate with generic clicking.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes four native tools for scope, capture-window search, diffs, and caseboard findings.
Frames show case scope text, agent panel, and transition toward evidence review.
execution_rationale: The product flow and UI are coherent, but contact-sheet frames show limited populated evidence results and not the full cited-diff completion.
execution_evidence: Frames show the Archive Evidence Room caseboard and agent-assisted scope workflow.
Packet describes exact captures, source excerpts, warnings, and Markdown export.
impact_rationale: Researchers, journalists, lawyers, and investigators have a concrete need to establish how webpages changed with source-grounded evidence.
impact_evidence: Packet frames the problem as manual archive archaeology and source checking.
Cited excerpts and bounded diffs directly support reviewable historical claims.
creativity_rationale: A page-history investigation room that keeps findings beside their sources is a memorable, well-pursued use of agent collaboration.
creativity_evidence: Shared caseboard rather than a detached chat answer.
Explicit untrusted-text warning and source-linked diff workflow.
usability_note: The caseboard framing and guided question are clear, but result details are small and sparse in the visible frames.
red_flags: Contact sheet does not clearly show populated archive results or final citations.
advance_reason: High WebMCP leverage and credible research value, despite incomplete visible end-state evidence.

one_line: Route-aware WebMCP tools for safe e-commerce operations and refund preparation.
what_it_does: Exposes structured tools across products, inventory, orders, customers, returns, and refunds while keeping publishing and final approval human-controlled.
leverage_rationale: Cross-module business state, versions, eligibility evidence, and route-aware tools make agent preparation safer and more precise than UI scraping.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes route-specific tools and structured identifiers, workflow stages, evidence, and versions.
Frames show refund queue and agent/tool-discovery narration.
execution_rationale: A complete refund-review path is specified and the frames show a coherent authenticated operations dashboard; final irreversible approval is intentionally human-gated.
execution_evidence: Frames show sign-in followed by populated refund operations dashboard.
Packet describes verify, draft reversible note, human publish/approval, and post-action rediscovery.
impact_rationale: Operations teams have a concrete need to process refund queues accurately while retaining auditability and control over consequential actions.
impact_evidence: Oldest pending approval is selected and evidence is verified before drafting.
High-risk publishing, approval, payment, and final results remain explicit human actions.
creativity_rationale: The route-aware, safety-bounded application layer is a strong product synthesis, though the underlying commerce dashboard category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Route-aware WebMCP discovery tied to the current page.
Reversible review-note preparation with human final authority.
usability_note: Familiar operations navigation and explicit approval boundaries support safe use; small callouts limit visual detail.
red_flags: Final refund state is not visibly completed in the contact sheet.
standouts: Excellent safety and workflow-boundary design for agentic commerce operations.
advance_reason: Strong real-world value, execution, and meaningful WebMCP delta.

one_line: Agent-native database schema diagramming on a shared visual canvas.
what_it_does: Extends drawDB with structured tools for schema generation, validation, SQL query checking, safe proposal-only deletion, checkpoints, and undo.
leverage_rationale: Validated atomic canvas edits, query checks, cascade previews, checkpoints, and shared undo provide meaningful precision and safety over DOM-driving a diagram editor.
leverage_evidence: Packet lists 17 WebMCP tools covering design, review, verification, removal, and checkpoints.
Frames show the diagram-editor shell and tooling context, though populated schema state is not legible.
execution_rationale: The described contract is thoughtful and coherent, but the contact sheet appears largely empty and does not visibly prove completed schema creation or validation.
execution_evidence: Frames show SchemaPair branding and an editor-like canvas with toolbar and inspector.
Packet claims one-prompt schema creation, validation, undo, query checking, and checkpoints.
impact_rationale: Developers and teams benefit materially from catching schema and query-design problems before migrations and downstream services.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies schema quality as foundational to services, queries, and migrations.
Index suggestions and production checks target concrete engineering risks.
creativity_rationale: Combining agent-native visual schema editing with proposal-only destructive changes and production checks is an original, safety-conscious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Whole-request validation lands as one undo step and pans to the change.
Agent shows cascade and requires human confirmation for deletion.
usability_note: Editor conventions and checkpoints suggest usability, but the visible canvas is sparse.
red_flags: Frames do not visibly show the claimed populated schema or completed agent action.
standouts: Strong safety primitives and validation concept.
advance_reason: Promising and high-value developer workflow, with execution confidence reduced by thin visible end-state evidence.

one_line: Agent-assisted procurement board for supplier qualification and tender-integrity screening.
what_it_does: Sweeps open procurement notices, extracts criteria, evaluates fit against a supplier profile, flags integrity concerns, and produces a dated bid plan on a shared board.
leverage_rationale: Batch dossier extraction and structured met/gap/unclear reasoning over shared procurement state are impractical to reproduce comparably through generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes one-button autonomous sweep over 12 notices with seven tools.
Frames show tender list, summary metrics, and a visible running agent activity panel.
execution_rationale: The frames visibly show a coherent dashboard moving from overview to batch processing with ordered agent activity, and the stated central workflow is complete for its scope.
execution_evidence: Frames show tender rows, summary cards, progress/status states, and right-side execution trace.
Packet reports criteria evidence, integrity flags, reasoning trace, and dated bid plan.
impact_rationale: Small suppliers face a specific capacity problem reading long tender dossiers; qualification and unfair-specification screening offers direct credible value.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies 40–130-page dossiers and limited staff as the target constraint.
Agent evaluates each criterion with attached evidence and flags narrow specifications.
creativity_rationale: The combination of supplier-fit scoring and integrity screening from the same procurement pass is unusually ambitious and socially meaningful.
creativity_evidence: Shared board mirrors every agent call and reasoning trace.
Live reranking after supplier-profile change demonstrates interactive decision support.
usability_note: One-button sweep with visible progress and trace is clear; dense tender data may require review discipline.
red_flags: Contact-sheet text is small, so individual dossier facts cannot be independently read.
standouts: Exceptional real-world problem fit and visible batch agent execution.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: transformative leverage, visible execution, and specific high-impact audience.

one_line: Agent turns music briefs into curated, editable playlists from a creator’s catalogue.
what_it_does: Searches a signed-in music catalogue against mood, tempo, vocal, and brief constraints, builds playlists, supports human listening/refinement, and prepares sharing.
leverage_rationale: Agents can translate briefs from elsewhere, search thousands of tracks, preserve playback context, and mutate the shared playlist while the human listens; generic UI work would be cumbersome.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes search, widening constraints, playlist mutation, playback-aware actions, and musical-marker navigation.
Frames show polished music landing/library views, though no readable agent panel.
execution_rationale: The transcript provides unusually clear end-to-end workflow evidence from brief to playlist, listening, removal, refinement, and sharing; silent frames cannot assess sonic quality.
execution_evidence: Transcript demonstrates initial three matches, expansion to eight, listening, remove-playing, and adding more options.
Frames show library grid and track table states.
impact_rationale: Music supervisors, producers, and artists with large catalogues have a concrete time-consuming discovery and pitching task.
impact_evidence: Packet targets catalogues of hundreds or thousands of unreleased tracks.
Workflow supports rediscovery, brief matching, listening validation, and private share links.
creativity_rationale: The agent collaborates with human taste during playback rather than replacing it, using moment-aware music actions in a compelling interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent can skip to loudest stretch or chorus and react to what is currently playing.
Human listens and decides while the agent continues constrained search.
usability_note: Playback-aware controls and incremental refinement fit creator workflows; exact agent UI is not visible.
red_flags: Audio quality, mixing, musicality, and timing feel are not assessable from silent frames.
Frames include Gmail and do not clearly show agent invocation UI.
standouts: Strong human-taste/agent-search collaboration and explicit end-to-end transcript.
advance_reason: Credible high-value creator workflow with strong transcript evidence; audio itself appropriately excluded from scoring.

one_line: Human-authorized decision engine where agents evaluate, challenge, negotiate, and justify recommendations.
what_it_does: Runs a staged decision protocol from research and scoring through explanation, challenge, negotiation, authorization, and commit, with human final authority.
leverage_rationale: The structured multi-stage decision state and explicit authorization boundary make agent collaboration materially more reliable than a generic answer or UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Packet specifies six native tools matching Evaluate → Explain → Challenge → Negotiate → Authorize → Commit.
Frames show weighted comparison, recommendation, challenge status, structured evidence, and approval-oriented controls.
execution_rationale: Frames depict a coherent configuration-to-recommendation-to-challenge flow with tool-like output; the final commit path is implied rather than fully visible.
execution_evidence: Frames show sliders, option comparisons, recommendation cards, red challenge state, and console-like evidence output.
Packet describes human approval before consequential commit.
impact_rationale: Teams making consequential choices need explainable recommendations and a clear boundary between reasoning and authorization.
impact_evidence: Product supports weighted priorities, tradeoffs, challenges, and human approval.
Frames visibly expose recommendation and validation states.
creativity_rationale: Making the agent defend and challenge its own decision before human authorization is a genuinely memorable interaction model pursued as a full protocol.
creativity_evidence: Explicit staged protocol rather than generic make-a-decision action.
Visual challenge/failure state and structured evidence support self-critique.
usability_note: Sliders, comparison cards, and approval gates communicate the staged flow, though dense dashboard text is small.
red_flags: Specific external tool names and final commit are not readable/visible in the contact sheet.
standouts: Clear distinction between recommendation and authorization, operationalized in the UX.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP concept with visible staged workflow and strong originality.

one_line: Workflow builder that turns business intent into validated WebMCP-ready service contracts.
what_it_does: Lets users and agents describe a workflow, choose an application shape, generate a Mantle manifest and service graph, preview API/MCP/WebMCP/Admin surfaces, and hand off implementation.
leverage_rationale: The agent directly authors validated structured service contracts and previews agent surfaces, rather than merely operating an existing UI; this is central to the product.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes four manifest atoms, validation, and generation of API, MCP, WebMCP, and Admin interfaces.
Frames show workflow-builder conversation, application-shape selection, nodes, and generated JSON/configuration.
execution_rationale: The visible flow reaches structured configuration and a workflow canvas, but the packet explicitly hands frontend/auth/deployment to a coding agent and does not show a deployed service.
execution_evidence: Frames show onboarding, shape selection, workflow nodes, and machine-readable output.
Packet states the handoff package guides completion rather than claiming all production surfaces are finished.
impact_rationale: Teams repeatedly building business workflows can reduce the gap between business rules and consistent agent-ready implementations.
impact_evidence: Packet targets trapped business logic, permissions, records, and operational workflows.
One contract is intended to power consumer, API, MCP, WebMCP, and admin surfaces.
creativity_rationale: A shared natural-language-to-contract builder for agent-ready business services is ambitious and distinctive, especially with one manifest spanning multiple surfaces.
creativity_evidence: Schema, View, Procedure, Trigger atoms form a coherent config-as-code model.
Application-shape selection plus generated service graph and JSON output is a novel interaction sequence.
usability_note: Guided shape selection and conversational setup help, but the generated configuration is developer-oriented and deployment is a handoff.
red_flags: No clear deployed production service or publish confirmation in visible frames.
standouts: Strong agent-infrastructure positioning with a concrete contract abstraction.
advance_reason: Highly differentiated infrastructure concept with visible generation flow, though not fully deployed in evidence.

one_line: Agent assembles a compatible, pickup-ready camping cart from one request with human confirmation.
what_it_does: Translates a camping mission into complete cart options, checks quantities, compatibility, price, stock, and pickup, reranks shared UI, and requires human confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Multi-product compatibility, budget, stock, pickup, and mission state are coordinated through structured tools and reflected in the same visible cart comparison.
leverage_evidence: Packet lists seven purpose-built tools and says agent calls update the same React storefront.
Frames visibly show tool-discovery and shared-UI mutation banners plus activity panel.
execution_rationale: The frames show progression from trip intake to product results with agent instrumentation; exact pickup receipt completion is described but not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show Woven landing, trip-builder, product grid, categories, and activity/status panels.
Packet reports two complete carts, seven units, five categories, packed volume, and human confirmation.
impact_rationale: First-time campers and similar shoppers have a real coordination problem assembling a complete compatible kit under practical constraints.
impact_evidence: Canonical mission includes two campers, one car boot, rain, budget/stock, and pickup today.
Results explain quantities, compatibility, prices, stock, and selected state.
creativity_rationale: The mission-oriented complete-cart model is more ambitious than product recommendation and keeps consent at the end of an agent-prepared workflow.
creativity_evidence: One request to two complete carts to pickup-ready order.
Human-only confirmation and merchant-approved alternatives preserve control.
usability_note: Trip intake, complete-cart comparison, and one review/confirm cycle are clear; dense shopping details are small in the sheet.
red_flags: Storefront is fictional/simulated, limiting evidence of real inventory beyond the demo.
Exact receipt details are not readable in contact sheet.
standouts: Strong end-to-end mission framing and explicit shared-state instrumentation.
advance_reason: Clear agent delta, visible product progression, and credible value for constrained multi-item shopping.
